snippets.harbor: The old harbor town sits where a slow river meets the sea. Fishing boats leave before dawn and return in the early afternoon, when the market along the quay fills with crates of mackerel, crabs and mussels. Behind the market a row of narrow houses climbs the hill, each painted a different color so that sailors could recognize their homes from the water. A lighthouse on the northern breakwater has guided ships for two hundred years, and its keeper still writes the weather into a logbook every evening. In summer the town hosts a festival where families race small wooden boats across the harbor, and the winner is allowed to ring the bell of the old customs house.
